title: Small filtered subsets under a cardinal power bound
statement: Use the smaller universe of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Fix a universe $\mathcal U$ and infinite regular cardinals $\alpha<\beta$ in $\mathcal U$. Suppose that $\mu^\nu<\beta$ for every cardinal $\mu<\beta$ and $\nu<\alpha$. Let $A$ be a small partially ordered set in which every subset of cardinality less than $\alpha$, including the empty subset, has an upper bound. Every subset $T\subseteq A$ with $|T|<\beta$ is contained in a subset $B\subseteq A$ with $|B|<\beta$ such that every subset of $B$ of cardinality less than $\alpha$ has an upper bound in $B$, with its inherited order. The poset $\mathscr B$ of all such $B$, ordered by inclusion, is small, covers $A$, and every family of fewer than $\beta$ elements of $\mathscr B$, including the empty family, has an upper bound in $\mathscr B$.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.2.8 and its transfinite closure proof, printed pp. 425-426; the two cardinals are written here as alpha (lower) and beta (upper). Read online, not archived under literature/. No Stacks tag states this cardinal-directedness lemma.

proof.text: For any small set $X$ with $\mu=|X|<\beta$, let $R_\xi$ be the family of ranges of all functions $\xi\to X$, for each ordinal $\xi<\alpha$ (viewing $\alpha$ as its initial ordinal). The range map is surjective onto $R_\xi$, so $|R_\xi|\leq\mu^{|\xi|}<\beta$ by the power hypothesis, since $|\xi|<\alpha$. Moreover $\mathcal P_{<\alpha}(X)=\bigcup_{\xi<\alpha}R_\xi$: each range has size at most $|\xi|$, and every subset of size $\nu<\alpha$ has a bijective enumeration by the initial ordinal of size $\nu$. The empty subset is the range of the unique function from $0$, including when $X=\varnothing$. There are $\alpha<\beta$ indices. The regular-cardinal union convention explicitly given in [lem-coef-small-directed-superset], applied to $\beta$, therefore gives $|\mathcal P_{<\alpha}(X)|<\beta$. Taking $E_X=\mathcal P_{<\alpha}(X)$ gives a cofinal family of this size: each member is contained in itself.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.2.8, successor-stage size bound, printed pp. 425-426; explicit range-counting argument supplying the cofinal-family hypothesis of the existing Mathlib leaf

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-small-directed-superset] with $(\sigma,\tau,I,S)=(\alpha,\beta,A,T)$. The cardinals are infinite regular with $\alpha<\beta$, Step 1 supplies its cofinal-family hypothesis for every small set of size less than $\beta$, and the assumed upper-bound condition on $A$ is exactly its poset $\alpha$-filteredness, including the empty subset. It produces $T\subseteq B\subseteq A$ with $|B|<\beta$ and with every subset of $B$ of size less than $\alpha$ bounded above in $B$. This is the asserted enlargement, in the inherited order.

source.place: Cardinal.SharplyLT.exists_isCardinalFiltered_set_of_exists_cofinal, lines 241-261; the existing leaf packages the transfinite closure construction of HTT Lemma 5.4.2.8

proof.text: The collection $\mathscr B$ is the subset of $\mathcal P(A)$ cut out by the stated size and upper-bound conditions. It is small because $A$ and its power set belong to the fixed universe, and inclusion restricts to a partial order on it. For every $a\in A$, the singleton $\{a\}$ has size $1<\beta$; Step 2 applied to it gives a member containing $a$. Thus $\bigcup_{B\in\mathscr B}B=A$. Step 2 applied to $T=\varnothing$ also gives a member of $\mathscr B$; it is nonempty even when proving the empty-family upper-bound clause.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.2.8, covering and family of all subsets; direct set-theoretic verification

proof.text: Let $\mathscr F\subseteq\mathscr B$ have $|\mathscr F|<\beta$, and set $T_{\mathscr F}=\bigcup_{C\in\mathscr F}C\subseteq A$. Every $C\in\mathscr F$ has size less than $\beta$, so the regular-cardinal union convention of [lem-coef-small-directed-superset] gives $|T_{\mathscr F}|<\beta$. Apply Step 2 to obtain $B\in\mathscr B$ containing $T_{\mathscr F}$. For every $C\in\mathscr F$, $C\subseteq T_{\mathscr F}\subseteq B$, so $B$ is an upper bound in the inclusion order. If $\mathscr F=\varnothing$, its union is empty and the same application of Step 2 supplies an upper bound. An indexed family with fewer than $\beta$ terms has fewer than $\beta$ distinct members, so this proves the assertion for families as well.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.2.8, final filtered-family assertion and the reduction to enlargements; regularity and explicit union argument
